newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold, platinum futures slip, others higher.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold, platinum futures slip, others higher.

text.p: Yen-based gold and platinum futures ended mostly lower on Monday, pressured by the yen's firmer tendency, while strong bullion prices helped silver and palladium futures to settle higher, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from flat to nine yen per gram weaker, with most-active benchmark December ending flat at 1,340 yen.
Activity was lacklustre with most individual investors sidelined amid the static currency market.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted firmer at $352.45/352.85 per ounce at 0718 GMT, against $352.30/352.80 in New York on Friday.

"Spot gold appears likely to find a floor for the near term, supported by the recent strength in silver. Although the fundamental tone in gold remains bearish on lingering fears about central bank sales, a short-term recovery is likely to correct the oversold conditions," one trader said.
Traders said the market would watch the U.S. stock market for possible further corrections.
In silver futures, trade houses, which covered short positions earlier, conducted fresh buying later, based on views that spot silver will reach $5.00 per ounce, they said.
Silver futures ranged from 0.2 yen to 4.5 yen per 10 grams higher, with benchmark December ending up 0.2 yen at 186.4 yen.
Benchmark December platinum futures settled two yen weaker at 1,354 yen. Palladium futures extended early gains to end higher, with three distant months hitting their life-of-contract highs.
Benchmark December palladium was up six yen at 468 yen.
"We have not yet heard any new information from the Russian platinum export agency. Palladium futures rose on constant physical buying, absorbing profit-taking," one trader said.
